chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatarri narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth.' He said: 'He commanded him to direct his face toward the Qibla, with nothing in it of the worship of idols, purely and sincerely.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse 'So set your face toward the religion' mean in the context of prayer direction?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the command to 'set your face toward the religion' (Surah Az-Zumar, 39:11) specifically mandates physical orientation toward the Qibla during prayer. He emphasizes that this act must be performed with *ikhlas* (sincerity), ensuring it is a pure act of worship distinct from the polytheistic practices of the pre-Islamic era. This interpretation highlights the transition from mere ritual direction to a holistic commitment to monotheism within Shia jurisprudence.
